alignments.note: The interrogative particle opening the rhetorical question takes the fronted auxiliary the ASV writes for it, rewritten over the coordinated second clause; both occurrences are its one discontinuous unit, headed on the first (rules 17 and 25).
One written negative whose scope covers both coordinated clauses; both *not*s belong to it (rule 25).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
Anarthrous substantival adjective recast as *him that was in trouble*; the supplied noun phrase and copula join its unit (rules 46 and 20), headed on *trouble*, which carries the lexeme of קָשֶׁה.
יוֹם of the idiom קְשֵׁה־יוֹם is left unwritten by the ASV's *him that was in trouble* (rule 22).
Finite verb *grieved*; the fronted *Was* is the question particle's (rule 17).
The article assimilated into the pointed preposition takes the written *the* (rule 12).

review_notes: Splitting קְשֵׁה־יוֹם, with *trouble* on the adjective and יוֹם unrepresented, was preferred to a `noncompositional` unit over both morphemes; the alternative is defensible and is named here under rule 8.
*Did* and *Was* are both given to the one אִם whose interrogative scope the ASV rewrites over the second clause (rule 25).
